faq: Can you move products from any platform?

We work with Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, Magento and CSV files from other tools. Digital products, subscriptions and customizers may need extra steps, which we flag before starting.
Will the product URLs stay the same?
Not always, because each platform builds its own link style. We keep the handles as close as possible and list every change. Redirects can be added through the Redirects and URLs service.
What happens to products that cannot be moved?
We list them in the report with the reason, for example unsupported product types or limits on variants. You decide whether to rebuild them by hand, replace them or leave them out.
Do you change my product descriptions?
No. We move your content as it is and only fix obvious problems like broken formatting. If you want better copy, we can quote that as a separate service after the move.

desc:
Product migration between ecommerce platforms moves your catalog to a new store with its detail intact. Ecom Swift LLC exports, cleans and imports your products, variants, images and collections in your own account, then checks a sample against the original.

## What is product migration?

Product migration is the transfer of your catalog from one store to another. A product is more than a name and a price. It includes a description, SKU, variants such as size and color, stock levels, images, categories, tags and search titles.

Every platform stores these items in its own format. A file exported from one cannot always be loaded into another without reshaping it first.

## Why catalogs go wrong during a move

Catalogs are messy by nature. Years of edits leave duplicate products, broken image links, inconsistent tags and variants with odd names. When that data is imported as it is, the problems come along, and some get worse because the new platform handles options differently.

A rushed import can also drop information silently. Variants merge into one product, images attach to the wrong item or descriptions lose their formatting. Nobody notices until a customer orders the wrong thing.

## How catalog quality affects sales

Products are what you sell, so errors here reach customers directly. A wrong price loses margin or trust. A missing variant means a shopper cannot choose the size they want. Poor images and thin descriptions lower the chance that anyone buys.

Collections and search fields matter too. Shoppers find products through categories, filters and the search bar. When tags and product types are carried over correctly, those tools work on day one. Clean titles and descriptions also help search engines understand each page.

## What a well-run product migration includes

- An export of the full catalog from the old platform.
- A review of the file for duplicates, empty fields and broken image links.
- Titles, descriptions, prices and SKUs mapped to the new fields.
- Variants built with correct options and stock levels.
- Images downloaded and attached to the right product and variant.
- Collections created, with rules where the new platform supports them.
- Tags, product types and vendors carried across.
- Search titles and descriptions kept.
- Custom fields mapped to metafields or the nearest equivalent.
- Image names and alt text tidied in the larger package.
- A line-by-line audit report of what moved and what did not.

## What we do

We begin by looking at the structure of your catalog and identifying anything that will behave differently on the new platform, such as option limits or bundle products. We clean the export, then import a small batch as a test.

We open those products and compare each field with the original. When the batch is correct, we load the full catalog and then check a sample, covering variants, prices, images and collections. Any item that cannot be moved exactly is listed, with an explanation and a suggested workaround.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in size and depth. Larger ones add variants and stock, tags and vendors, custom fields, related products and the audit report.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Remove products you will never sell again.
- Keep SKUs unique and consistent.
- Gather your original image files if you have them.
- Decide how collections should be organized.
- Review a sample of imported products yourself.

**Avoid:**
- Importing a catalog full of duplicates.
- Letting image links point back to the old store.
- Changing prices during the transfer.
- Assuming every custom field has a home.
- Rewriting every description before the move.

## Who this is for

An owner changing platforms with a catalog too large to retype. A seller who has combined several suppliers into one messy export. A brand adding variants and collections that need to be rebuilt in a cleaner structure.

## What we need from you

Provide the old store address and either a product export or a staff or collaborator user on the old store. Tell us about unusual items such as bundles, subscriptions or made-to-order goods.

We never ask for passwords. The new store stays in your account, so the finished catalog belongs to you from the start.
